title: UPDATE 4-Run on Corpbank prompts Bulgarian  central bank  to seize control
text:
* Follows reports of shady deals involving top shareholder

* Central bank to take control for three months

* Says no fear of contagion to other lenders

* Hungary's OTP, Greece's NBG both say no impact on ops

* Bulgarian credit default swaps rise to 6-month high (Adds banker and depositor quotes, details, background, market close)

By Matthias Williams and Tsvetelia Tsolova

SOFIA, June 20 (Reuters) - A run on Corporate Commercial Bank (Corpbank) prompted Bulgaria's central bank to take control of the country's fourth-largest lender on Friday and its governor appealed to depositors to stay calm.

The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said it would handle Corpbank's operations for three months and removed its management and supervisory board after the run, which was sparked by media reports of shady deals involving the bank.

The BNB said it acted after Corpbank said on Friday morning it had stopped all payments and bank operations due to a liquidity drain. The central bank said Corpbank was not bankrupt and other lenders in the country were safe from the effects.

"As you know, there has been a lot of talk about the bank and one of its shareholders, which triggered bank runs," central bank governor Ivan Iskrov said at a news conference. "It is very important to be very careful when we talk about banks. Let's not tear down our house alone unnecessarily."

"Let me make this very clear. Corporate Commercial Bank is not a bankrupt bank. We are acting swiftly to avoid a bankruptcy," said Iskrov.

He declined to give further details of the bank's problems and said supervisors would carry out a full audit of its books.

The central bank action did not stop dozens of people from queuing outside the main office of the bank in the capital Sofia on Friday, and credit default swaps on the country's debt hit a six-month high on fears of contagion. Sofia's blue-chip shares index closed at its lowest level since February.

The central bank blocked depositors from withdrawing cash after it took control.

"We are worried, because my husband and I have deposits there in euros and in U.S. dollars," said Lilia Polova, editor at a lifestyle magazine. "These are our family savings. He was reading newspapers and was asking me to take our money out of there ... but I waited."

Bulgaria's stock exchange suspended Corpbank from trading and the country's financial regulator ordered that the shares remain suspended until Wednesday next week in order to protect investors and stabilise the market.

LETTER LEAKED

Iskrov said Corpbank depositors stepped up withdrawals after an anonymous letter leaked to Bulgarian media said the central bank's deputy governor in charge of banking supervision was being investigated by prosecutors for abuse of office.

The central bank has since confirmed the investigation and said the deputy governor had taken a voluntary leave of absence.

Reports in Bulgarian media linked the investigation of the deputy governor to allegations of corruption at Corpbank.

In an interview with a Bulgarian TV news channel, whose contents were published by Corpbank on Thursday, Corpbank's top shareholder Tsvetan Vassilev denied any wrongdoing on his part or the bank's.

"We are a responsible bank both towards our client depositors and Bulgarian business," he said. Corpbank said on Thursday that Vassilev was ready to cooperate with the investigation into the bank's affairs.

A spokeswoman for Corpbank said on Friday that she was not allowed to make statements without the central bank's approval. She said she did not know Vassilev's whereabouts and in any case would not be allowed to share such information.

The leading shareholders in the Sofia-listed bank are Vassilev, with just over half the company, Oman's sovereign wealth fund with around 30 percent and Russia's VTB Asset Management with nearly 10 percent, Thomson Reuters data showed.

Friday's move by the central bank was the first such intervention since Bulgaria's 1996-1997 financial crisis, which led to the bankruptcies of 14 Bulgarian banks and forced the introduction of a currency board regime in the country.

SITUATION "ISOLATED"

The bank run comes at a bad time for Bulgaria's government, which is preparing for an early election after the ruling Socialists suffered a bad result in European Parliament elections and a junior coalition partner withdrew its support.

Political instability in the European Union's poorest state has smothered reforms needed to spur economic growth and tackle high employment. Standard and Poor's downgraded Bulgaria's sovereign credit ratings last week to a notch above junk.

The government said it was ready to support efforts to stabilise Corpbank. Shareholder VTB also expressed interest in lending support, and the central bank said talks with VTB would start immediately.

Iskrov was quick to play down concerns that the panic could spread to other lenders in the region, which sits on the edge of a euro zone still recovering from its own financial crisis.

He said Bulgaria's banking system was not interlinked enough for Corpbank's problems to spread.

There are 29 commercial banks operating in Bulgaria and some three quarters of the banking system's assets are foreign-owned. Among foreign banks with operations in Bulgaria are UniCredit , Raiffeisen Bank, Hungary's OTP, National Bank of Greece, Eurobank and Alpha Bank.

OTP said the situation was "isolated", and National Bank of Greece and Eurobank both said their Bulgarian units were not experiencing any problems.

Bulgarian bank deposits in local and foreign currency are guaranteed up to 196,000 levs ($136,600), or 100,000 euros by law. The central bank will launch talks with shareholders to calculate the support the bank will need, Iskrov said.

"There is no spillover effect. I think that if the central bank and the government take fast measures there will be none," said Levon Hampartzoumian, chief executive of Unicredit Bulbank, Bulgaria's largest lender and head of the Association of Commercial Banks in Bulgaria.

"There is no similarity to the 1996 crisis, when there were serious cross-banking exposures," he told Reuters.

($1 = 1.4349 Bulgarian Levs) (Writing by Pravin Char and Simon Jessop; editing by Tom Pfeiffer)

title: CEE MARKETS 4-Poland  intervention ,  Bulgaria  ERM-2 delay hit  FX
text:
* Zloty knocked down by central bank intervention

* Bulgaria drops ERM-2 entry plans, mkt spooked

* Investors in wait-and-see mode ahead of Hungary election

(Updates throughout)

By Marius Zaharia and Dagmara Leszkowicz

BUCHAREST/WARSAW, April 9 (Reuters) - The zloty fell on Friday after the Polish central bank's first intervention in 10 years, while other central European currencies were pressured by Bulgaria's decision to delay its euro plans after revealing a hidden budget deficit.

Poland's central bank said in a statement it bought foreign currencies in the market, following a string of comments from officials this week trying to talk the zloty down. [ID:nWSF008905] [ID:nLDE63806P]

The central bank's deputy governor Witold Kozinski said later in the day the bank could not rule out further interventions in the currency market. [ID:nWSF008910]

The intervention raised concerns that policymakers in other central European countries might favour undervalued currencies to help economies recover from their worst recession in decades.

"There is a sentiment others will do the same as Poland. Romania has already done it and now investors are encouraged to think more ... is to come," a dealer in Bucharest said.

Another case of regional contagion occurred after Bulgaria announced it was delaying plans to enter the ERM-2 euro entry waiting zone because of unaccounted procurement deals that have widened the deficit to 3.7 percent of GDP last year from an initial 1.9 percent gap. [ID:nLDE63813A] [ID:nLDE63813L]

Dealers in Romania said investors became concerned that other countries in central Europe could have hidden deficits like Greece, and the leu was worst hit by the Bulgarian news. [ID:nBUC003670]

"Obviously, we may see a deterioration of investor sentiment. We've already seen an impact on the leu," said Melania Hancila, chief economist at Volksbank in Bucharest.

"I do believe that investors will be very carefully assessing data coming from Romania and other countries in the region. CDS quotations may rise because of this situation in Bulgaria."

At 1413 GMT, the zloty <EURPLN=> was down 0.6 percent at 3.871 per euro, off almost two-week lows hit earlier in the session.

The leu <EURRON=> was down 0.5 percent, while the Czech crown <EURCZK=> was almost flat and Hungary's forint <EURHUF=> gained 0.3 percent from Thursday's close.

HUNGARY'S ELECTION

Hungarians will vote on Sunday in the first round of an election that looks set to bring a landslide victory for the opposition centre-right Fidesz party, giving it a strong mandate for reforms. [ID:nLDE6351AW]

Fidesz, which campaigned on tax cuts and job creation, could even secure a two-thirds majority, which would empower the party to pass broader structural reforms.

"The market is in a wait-and-see mode," one trader in Budapest said. "Indications for a chance of a two-thirds majority (for opposition party Fidesz) on Sunday could reassure markets and be mildly forint positive."

Hungarian bonds were steady, and analysts say their bull run may continue after the election as an expected strong majority government, a supply squeeze and hopes for more rate cuts bode well [ID:nLDE62U1OZ].

The forint, however, is set to give up some ground in the next few months after the elections, a monthly Reuters poll showed on Friday, but is poised for a modest gain of less than 1 percent over a 12-month horizon.[ID:nLDE6380S7]

title: UPDATE 1-Bulgaria c.bank says FIBank in "excellent condition"
text:
(Adds central bank governor, FIBank comment, paragraphs 5-8)

SOFIA, May 16 (Reuters) - Bulgaria's central bank said First Investment Bank (FIBank) and other Bulgarian banks were in "excellent condition", dismissing rumours it faced financial problems.

Rumours have spread via several Bulgarian Internet blogs in the past two weeks that FIBank, Bulgaria's sixth largest bank by assets, had problems. That led to deposit withdrawals in the past few days, a central bank spokesman said.

"The governing board of the BNB (Bulgaria's central bank) categorically confirms that all Bulgarian banks, including FIBank are in an excellent condition with high liquidity and normal credit levels," the central bank said in a statement.

"The BNB will not allow FIBank to fall into trouble on the basis of unfounded rumours," the statement said.

FIBank said a separate statement later on Friday that deposit withdrawals, which surged in the past two days, had now fallen sharply.

"The crisis caused by the rumours has been overcome and client trust in the bank will recover in the next few days," said the bank, most of which is privately held, said.

Local news agency Focus quoted central bank governor Ivan Iskrov as saying that the spread of the rumours was a "scenario" aiming at damaging FIBank's credibility.

The central bank will ask prosecutors to investigate the case, Iskrov said.

Bulgarians still have bitter memories of a 1996/97 financial crisis that wiped out a third of the Balkan country's banks. The European Union newcomer has since introduced a currency board regime that pegs the national currency to the euro.

FIBank had assets worth of 4.07 billion levs ($3.22 billion) at end-March, when it posted a net profit of 15.07 million levs up from 10.1 million profit a year ago.

Bulgarian banks have enjoyed a credit boom in the past few years as people sought debt to buy consumer goods like flat screen TVs, new cars and houses after decades of communist austerity.

Loans grew 62.5 percent last year, while deposits rose by 34.3 percent, central bank data showed.

The central bank, worried by the credit boom, urged banks late last year to raise lending rates and tighten rules. It has said it was ready to intervene with fresh measures to cool the trend.

Bulgaria's 29 banks are mainly owned by big European lenders, many from Italy, Austria, Germany and Greece. (Reporting by Anna Mudeva and Tsvetelia Ilieva; editing by Rory Channing)

title: Bulgaria  lev/dlr firms on ECB  intervention  fears.
text:
SOFIA, Nov 10 (Reuters) - Bulgaria's lev gained against the dollar at Friday's close, reflecting euro's rise as markets feared the European Central Bank might step in again to support the euro after three interventions in the past week. 

 "Trade was mainly client-driven today with companies mostly buying dollars, but some banks remained sidelined wary of a new intervention," a bank dealer said. 

 The lev ended the week at 2.245/2.247 per dollar, from 2.271/2.172 on Thursday, reflecting euro's rebound against the dollar on global markets through the lev/euro peg. 

 On Thursday, the ECB stepped into global markets to sell both dollars and yen to prop up the single currency in the third unilateral intervention in the past week. 

 Against the euro, the lev ended at 1.9463/1.9466, from 1.9461/1.9464 on Thursday as banks covered the rise in client dollar demand through euro/dollar arbitrage deals. 

 Bulgaria pegged the lev at 1.95583 per euro from 1999 as part of the currency board system.

title: Bulgaria  lev gains vs dollar on ECB  intervention .
text:
SOFIA, Nov 10 (Reuters) - Bulgaria's lev erased part of losses against the dollar on Friday morning, shadowing euro's rise versus the U.S. currency after the European Central Bank intervened late on Thursday to support its currency. 

 "I expect clients to be bullish on the dollar today but some market players are likely to wait for a further fall in the dollar as the ECB is likely to keep buying euros and the Bank of Japan can join it," a bank dealer said. 

 The lev opened at 2.239/2.241 per dollar, from 2.271/2.172 at Thursday's close, reflecting euro's rebound against the dollar on global markets overnight through the lev/euro peg. 

 On Thursday, the ECB stepped in to sell both dollars and yen to lift the single currency in the third unilateral intervention in the past week. 

 Against the euro, the lev opened at 1.9463/1.9466, from 1.9461/1.9464 late on Thursday as banks prepared to cover the expected rise in client dollar demand through euro/dollar arbitrage deals. 

 Bulgaria pegged the lev at 1.95583 per euro from 1999 as part of the currency board system.

title: BULGARIA LEV CLOSES DOWN 37 PCT FROM END-1996.
text:
SOFIA, Jan 4 (Reuter) - The Bulgarian lev lost 37 percent in the first two trading days of 1997 for the local interbank market, closing at a new record low of 695-698 per dollar on Saturday in extremely thin volume, dealers said. 

 The lev opened at 620-660 per dollar and traded at 640-650 at midday, down from 590-605 at Friday's close and from 507-510 on Monday, the last trading day of 1996 for the local market before the New Year recess. 

 "Big final clients bid for large foreign currency volumes while banks and clients alike were reluctant to sell amid an ongoing lev slide," a commercial bank dealer said. 

 "Final clients bought every dollar offered irrespective of the high price," another dealer said. 

 The central bank was not seen selling dollars to support the crumbling lev, traders said. Central bank officials were not available for comment. 

 Markets were closed in Bulgaria from Tuesday through Thursday for the New Year. 

 Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Sunday that BNB powers to counter pressure on the lev through interventions were limited because payments on Bulgaria's foreign debt in 1997 would be a priority for the BNB. 

 Low BNB foreign exchange reserves, lack of financing from abroad and lower than expected privatisation proceeds in 1996 were the reasons why the central bank could not prevent the lev decline, Filipov said. 

 BNB forex reserves stood at $525 million at the end of November last year, down from $1.408 billion a year earlier. 

 Bulgaria has to meet some $300 million of foreign debt payments in the first quarter with $170-180 million due in January alone. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032

title: Bulgaria lev loses 18 pct versus dlr in day.
text:
SOFIA, Jan 3 (Reuter) - The Bulgarian lev closed between 590-605 per dollar on Friday, down from 575-585 in the morning and 507-510 at Monday's close as dollar demand topped supply in light interbank volume, dealers said. 

 The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) was not seen selling dollars to halt the lev slide during the first trading day of 1997 for the local interbank market, dealers said. 

 BNB officials were not available for comment. Local markets were closed from Tuesday through Thursday for the New Year. 

 "The lev lost some 18 percent on the day because dollar demand coming mainly from small final clients heavily outweighed supply," a commercial bank dealer said. @ 

 Trade was very thin in the afternoon because there were just a few foreign currency bidders left in the market while dollar supply rose slightly due to profit taking, helping the lev consolidate near 600 per dollar, another trader said. 

 "Dollar rates above 600 per dollar were deemed too high at the moment and many bidders withdrew from the market in the afternoon," the second dealer said. 

 BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Sunday that BNB powers to counter pressure on the lev through interventions were limited because payments on Bulgaria's foreign debt in 1997 would be a priority for the BNB. 

 Low BNB foreign exchange reserves, lack of financing from abroad and lower than expected privatisation proceeds in 1996 were the reasons why the central bank could not prevent a lev decline, Filipov said. 

 BNB forex reserves stood at $525 million at the end of November last year. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032

title: Bulgaria lev slumps to 575-585 per dollar.
text:
SOFIA, Jan 3 (Reuter) - The Bulgarian lev slumped to 575-585 per dollar in low interbank volume on the first trading day of 1997 from 507-510 at the close on December 30 as foreign currency demand heavily topped supply, dealers said. 

 "A commercial bank and a financial house have been aggressively bidding for dollars since the opening, buying every dollar on offer irrespective of the ask price," a commercial bank dealer said. 

 The dollar was bid around 595 levs around 1030 local time (0830 GMT), but no one offered foreign currency below 610, traders said. 

 Dealers said they were unsure whether financial institutions bought dollars for final clients or built up forex positions in anticipation of a pending sharp lev fall in the absence of central bank support for the national currency. 

 The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) was not seen intervening in the market by mid-morning, traders said. BNB officials were not available for comment 

 BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Sunday that BNB powers to counter pressure on the lev through interventions were limited because payments on Bulgaria's foreign debt in 1997 would be a priority for the BNB. @ 

 Low BNB foreign exchange reserves, lack of financing from abroad and lower than expected privatisation proceeds in 1996 were the reasons why the central bank could not prevent a lev decline, Filipov said. 

 Filipov said Bulgaria has to pay some $170-180 million coupon on its Brady bonds on January 28. 

 BNB forex reserves stood at $525 million at the end of November last year. 

 -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032

title: BULGARIA  LEV WEAKENS AS C.BANK FAILS TO  INTERVENE .
text:
SOFIA, Dec 4 (Reuter) - The Bulgarian lev closed at a new all-time low of 415-418 per dollar after 395-400 in the morning as the central bank (BNB) was not seen supporting it amid a persistently high foreign currency demand, dealers said. 

 "Fuel importers were bidding for relatively large dollar volumes but supply from banks was low and the lev lost some 30 (levs per dollar) on the day after the central bank failed to intervene," a commercial bank dealer said. 

 BNB officials declined comment. 

 The lev closed around 386-387 on Tuesday on the interbank market. It traded at 362-364 per dollar on Monday. 

 Commercial banks were reluctant to sell dollars in anticipation of a further lev fall amid unsatisfied foreign currency demand from final clients, dealers said. 

 Traders said the exchange rate was not moved by a BNB decisison on Wednesday to continue to participate on the local market to support the lev. 

 "The BNB does not have much room left to prevent a lev slide through interventions after its reserves fell again last month," another dealer said. 

 BNB foreign exchange reserves fell by $15.7 million to $525.1 million in November, the BNB said in a statement. 

 Reserves stood near $1.41 billion in November 1995 and have steadily declined since then due to payments on Bulgaria's foreign debt and BNB interventions in support of the lev. 

 The BNB also said on Wednesday it had decided to step up supervision to ensure that commercial banks adhere to its regulations requiring banks to have a maximum ratio of 30 percent between their net open foreign currency positions and their own funds. 

 The previous low for the lev of 395 per dollar was on November 21. The lev traded near 70 to the dollar at the beginning of 1996. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032

title: Bulgaria  c.bank says  interventions  continue.
text:
SOFIA, Dec 4 (Reuter) - The Bulgarian National Bank said in a statement on Wednesday it will continue intervening on the local interbank forex market to support the slumping lev. 

 The cash-strapped central bank has carried out modest interventions on the local forex market in the past month to prop up the lev, which fell from 246 to the dollar on November 4 to a record low 413 per dollar on Wednesday. 

 "In order to support the national currency, the BNB will continue to participate on the foreign exchange market," said the statement. 

 The BNB board, which will continue its session on Thursday, is also expected to step up supervision to ensure that commercial banks adhere to regulations requiring banks to have a maximum ratio of up to 30 percent between their net open foreign currency positions and their own funds, said the statement. 

 Bulgaria is currently debating the introduction of a tight financial regime, called a currency board system, to resolve a grave economic crisis caused by delayed reform and siphoning of capital abroad. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561

title: BULGARIA  LEV SLUMPS AS C.BANK HALTS  INTERVENTIONS .
text:
SOFIA, Nov 20 (Reuter) - The Bulgarian lev slumped to 330-335 per dollar from 229 in the morning after foreign currency supply thinned down to a trickle and the central bank did not intervene to support the lev, dealers said. 

 "The (interbank) market was listless in the afternoon because most traders retreated to the sidelines after the lev nosedived to 330-335," a commercial bank dealer said. 

 Dealers said an insurance company was bidding for large foreign currency volumes for pending payments of dollar-denominated reinsurance fees, strongly pressuring the lev amid an almost non-existing dollar supply. 

 The central bank did not intervene to support the lev like it was doing for most of November so far, dealers said. 

 A central bank official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters the bank planned to save its dwindling forex reserves for the possible introduction of a currency board and for foreign debt payments rather than for propping up the lev. 

 Additional pressure over the lev came from the cash market, where Bulgarians converted lev savings into hard currency, dealers said. 

 The dollar was offered at 345-350 levs at exchange bureaux in early afternoon, but lack of demand at these levels made sellers lower their asks for the dollar to 325-330 levs later on, traders said. 

 Individuals have withdrawn some 13 billion levs from the State Savings Bank since the middle of last week until Tuesday, part of which were probably channeled to the cash forex market, Bistra Dimitrova, head of the SSB told Reuters. 

Central bank (BNB) foreign exchange reserves reserves stood near $541 million at the end of October, down from $1.434 billion a year ago, BNB figures show. 

 Apart from foreign exchange reserves the central bank manages gold reserves worth some $400 million. 

 Dues to government and bank creditors in the first quarter of 1997 total $300 million or some 30 percent of all debt payments for next year. 

 A month ago BNB experts estimated Bulgaria would need some $200-300 million for fuel and food imports by the year-end. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032

title: Bulgaria  Lev/BNB  Intervenes  -4: Mineralbank Bonds
text:
Obretenov said the central bank had failed to intervene in April, instead increasing interest rates to 108%. And he doubts how long they will be able to intervene. 'Their reserves are too thin,' he said. 

 Moreover, the IMF has made it a condition of further lending that Bulgaria maintain its foreign exchange reserves, he added. 

 'I think tomorrow (Friday) will be the last day they come in to check rates,' Obretenov said of the central bank. 'For the next month they won't be in and the dollar will go slowly, slowly higher.' 

 The increase in fuel prices, VAT and other measures aimed at raising revenue are certain to push up inflation, traders argued. 

 While international investors are calm at the moment that Bulgaria will continue servicing its foreign debts, investors who bought privately-placed bonds issued in 1989 by the bankrupt Mineralbank are worried they won't be repaid when the 5 billion yen in bonds mature June 14. The state closed Mineralbank May 17. 

 Talk in Sofia, however, is that the bank has sufficient reserves in Swiss francs in a Swiss bank to cover the bonds, and in the event it doesn't, that the government could take the debt on as state debt, a trader said, citing a contact at Mineralbank. 

 And on the domestic side, despite the crushing burden of high rates, National Bank Governor Filipov said it's not possible to cut the base rate, given current exchange rates, according to BTA. The rate can be lowered only in case the tendency is reversed, he added. 

 Overall, said Obretenov, 'the situation is really bad.'

title: Bulgaria  Lev/BNB  Intervenes  -3:  Forex  Reserves Are Thin
text:
The central bank also moved to limit the amount of minimum reserves commercial banks could withdraw. 

 'This is a complex of measures to stabilize the forex market, given that demand considerably exceeds supply,' National Bank Governor Lyubomir Filipov told parliament Wednesday. 

 The central bank intervention was small by world standards, perhaps, but dealers pointed out that the Bulgarian market, is small, under developed, and easily moved by what in more mature markets would be small amounts. 'The problem with our market is that it's small and not liquid,' the Postbank dealer said. 

 And volatile. 'We started at 170, went to 210 then came to 150,' Obretenov said. 'Normal people are nervous,' he said. Customers who bought dollars at 200 to 210 leva are now asking 'how can we cancel the deal,' he added. 

 The outlook for the lev remains far from rosy. The one result of the intervention seems to be that the lev won't fall as rapidly against the dollar as it has in recent weeks. But it seems certain it will continued to depreciate. 'Nobody wants to sell dollars. Everybody wants to buy dollars,' Obretenov said. 

 While the market is calm now, how long that - and the lev's recovery against the dollar - will last 'depends on the central bank,' said the Postbank dealer. 'If not too many buyers appear, the market could go to 150' leva per dollar he said, adding he doesn't expect it to climb again to 200 leva per dollar.

title: Bulgaria  Lev/BNB  Intervenes  -2: Mkt Doubted It Would Act
text:
The Bulgarian lev has suffered badly in the current economic crisis, slipping to 161.97 leva per dollar from 70.704 leva per dollar at the end of 1995. The lev recovered at Thursday's fixing, whose rate is used for statistical and reference purposes, rising to 147.04 leva per dollar. 

 After signing a memorandum of intent with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the Bulgarian government Wednesday and Thursday announced a series of price increases for energy, higher value-added taxes (VAT) and a 5% import duty to compliment efforts to close loss-making enterprises and insolvent banks. 

 The country's foreign exchange reserves fell to $670 at the end of April from more than $1.2 billion at the end of 1995 as the country made payments on some $1.2 billion of foreign debt servicing due this year. 

 As reserves fell, the central bank refrained from intervening to support the lev. Thus market participants were surprised when the BNB stepped into the market Wednesday and again Thursday. 

 'I don't think the market believed they would intervene,' said the trader at the Bulgarian Postbank. 

 The central bank governing board Wednesday decided to stop funding commercial banks, limiting the inflow of leva that they might use to purchase hard currency. The central bank also raised rates on security repurchase agreements, the state news agency BTA reported.

title: Bulgaria  Lev Around 140 Leva/Dlr After BNB  Intervenes
text:
PRAGUE (AP-Dow Jones)--The Bulgarian lev settled around 140 leva per dollar Thursday after two days of heavy intervention by the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB), dealers in Sofia said. 

 The interventions took the market by surprise Wednesday, when the dollar was offered as high as 210 leva on Bulgaria's thin and nervous foreign exchange market, dealers said. 

 The Bulgarian National Bank spent some $7 million to $10 million of its precious - and dwindling - foreign exchange reserves Wednesday and another $3 million to $5 million Thursday in interventions on the market, estimates Lyubomir Obretenov, chief dealer at First East International Bank in Sofia. 

 The 'Continent' newspaper quoted Stoyan Shoukerov, head of the central bank's foreign operations department, as saying that when the dollar reached 190 to 195 leva, the central bank sold $4 to $4.5 million. 

 Dealers said Wednesday's intervention knocked the dollar down to 150 to 155 leva. 

 Thursday, the central bank sold dollars at 150 leva, 145 leva and 140 leva, with the dollar finally settling at 135 to 140 leva at the close of trading Thursday. 

 A dealer at the Bulgarian Postbank said he expects the lev Friday at near the same level, quoting a spread of 130 to 140 leva per dollar. 

 'I think 135-140 (leva per dollar) is the low,' said Obretenov, adding, '140 is a very, very good level to buy.'

title: Bulgaria  c-bank to support lev with  interventions .
text:
SOFIA, May 29 (Reuter) - The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said in a statement on Wednesday it would intervene on the local interbank forex market to support the lev. 

 "The BNB board decided to launch unlimited interventions from May 29 on the foreign exchange market in support of the national currency," said the statement, released after an extraordinary board meeting. 

 Direct dollar sales launched by the BNB at noon on Wednesday helped the lev recover to 140-145 by mid-afternoon from historic lows of 200 per dollar in early morning bids for foreign currency. 

 Several Bulgarian commercial banks joined the BNB's dollar sales during the afternoon, offering dollars on sale orders by final clients eager to sell while the dollar was expensive. 

 The lev closed at 150-160 per dollar after the BNB halted its dollar offers. 

 Many dealers expressed doubts about the BNB's power to prop up the lev with interventions alone because of its severely limited foreign exchange reserves. 

 BNB governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Tuesday that the central bank would have to curb its interventions on the domestic interbank market in line with pledges made to the International Monetary Fund (IMF). 

 The Fund has asked Bulgaria to boost its foreign exchange reserves under a preliminary funding deal agreed on Monday. 

 BNB forex reserves have fallen to around $500 million according to unofficial estimates. Bulgaria faces foreign debt payments of some $700 million in July alone. 

 Filipov did not say how the BNB planned to raise its forex reserves. 

 -- Gareth Jones, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-328101

title: Brady Bond Market: Russia Rises On Bank Meeting, Polls
text:
LONDON (Dow Jones)--Russian loans continued to rise on the market for developing country debt Wednesday, pushed higher by news of a meeting between the country's debt negotiators and its foreign bank creditors. 

 Recent improvements in President Boris Yeltsin's standing in the polls have also helped, traders said. 

 Vneshekonombank U.S. dollar loans gained one point on the offer side to 38.5 on news that a Russian delegation will meet with the country's Bank Advisory Committee (BAC) in London next Monday. The meeting is expected to produce a term sheet outlining the precise details of the debt rescheduling agreement negotiated in November. 

 Once agreed, the term sheet will be presented to Russia's 400 creditor banks for their approval, a significant step towards completing the agreement. 

 Recent polls which have shown Yeltsin gaining ground on Gennady Zyuganov, his main rival in June's presidential elections, have also helped boost Russian debt prices. 

 One poll published Monday gave Yeltsin a slight lead over the Communist Party candidate. It was the first nationwide poll to do so. 

 Elsewhere in eastern Europe, Bulgarian Brady bonds edged slightly higher on hopes that the country will soon conclude agreements with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank which will improve its ability to repay its foreign debt. 

 Bulgarian Discount bonds rose by 1/8 to 51.875 bid. 

 The market shrugged off the continuing decline in the rate of exchange of the Lev against the dollar. Dealers in Sofia said the National Bank of Bulgaria was unable to intervene in support of the Lev because it doesn't have enough foreign exchange reserves. The central bank's reserves stood at $700 million at the end of March.

The central bank tried twice this year to stop the steep rise of the dollar and protect the savings in local currency by raising the base interest rate to 49% currently from 34% at the end of last year. 

 But hopes that interest in hard currency would fade and that the central bank was in control were dashed. 'Our country needs foreign exchange for payments and to buy goods,' Varbarnov said. 

 Bankers maintain that the central bank's monetary measures are ineffective and that other financial mechanisms have to be found. 

 The central bank didn't intervene Tuesday or Wednesday, and Varbarnov said it's indicated that it won't intervene 'because it doesn't have money for the intervention.' 

 Official foreign exchange reserves dropped to around $900 million early this year from $1.2 billion at the end of 1995; they dropped further to $700 million at the end of March in part as Bulgaria made a regular payment to the commercial and official creditors under agreements. 

 Bulgaria owes some $1.2 billion in 1996 in principle and interest repayments. Officials expect a trade surplus of around $400 million and a current account surplus of $100 million in 1996. 

 'On this basis we hope in the spring and the summer to improve our reserves,' Filipov said. 

 The lev's depreciation reflects the difficulties which Bulgaria meets while trying to reform its communist-built economy along market lines. 'The big problem is in the economy,' Varbarnov said. While he said he thinks the government will be able to carry out its restructuring plans, 'this is very difficult and will go very slowly.'

title: BULGARIAN LEV FALLS TO ALL-TIME LOW OF 91 VS DLR.
text:
SOFIA, April 24 (Reuter) - The Bulgarian lev shed 3.4 percent on Wednesday to close at an all-time low of 91.00 per dollar due to very low supply of foreign currency on the interbank forex market, dealers said. 

 "We sold a small amount of dollars at 91 levs in late afternoon," a commercial bank dealer said, adding that a demand for some $1.5 million by the same buyer had remained unsatisfied by the close. 

 The local branch of a foreign bank has actively bid for dollars throughout the day, attracting the scarce offers at increasingly higher lev rates, traders said. 

 Most banks, worried by the sharp lev fall, refrained from trading in the market and preferred to strike deals mainly with final clients, dealers said. 

 "Traders have lost confidence in each other after forex trade was disrupted earlier this week by cancellation of forward contracts," another commercial bank dealer said. 

 At least two financial brokerages have cancelled payments since last week on forward contracts, putting banks with short dollar positions in a difficult situation. 

 This pushed most banks out of the market, which in turn made trade very thin and volatile with the bid/ask spread widening to three to four levs. 

 The central bank was not sighted trading in the market, dealers said, adding that shrinking forex reserves and uncertainty over funding deals with the international lending institutions continue to weigh heavily on the lev. 

Central bank forex reserves fell by $201 million to $703 million in March. They stood at $1.3 billion in December before Bulgaria had to make Brady coupon interest payments, interest payments to the Paris Club of creditor governments and interventions in support of the lev. 

Bulgaria has to pay a total of $1.2 billion on its foreign debt this year. This is expected to stretch Sofia's finances to the limit if it fails to strike fresh funding deals with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, analysts said. 

 The IMF and the World Bank are currently scrutinising the small print of a reform programme handed over by Bulgaria's socialist government nearly two weeks ago. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-328101

title: Bulgarian lev recovers to 83.00 vs dlr at close.
text:
SOFIA, April 18 (Reuter) - A moderate rise of dollar supply helped the Bulgarian lev recover to around 83.00 per dollar at the close of the interbank market on Thursday, from its record low of 83.70 in late morning trade, dealers said. 

 "A large commercial bank offered a relatively small amount of dollars in early afternoon at levels around 83.00 levs and the market settled there until the close," a commercial bank dealer said. 

 Low supply of foreign currency due to market worries over a sharp fall in forex reserves and uncertainty whether Bulgaria will strike much-needed funding deals with the IMF and the World Bank pressured the lev, dealers said. 

 "In a market as thin as today's every dip in supply or demand brings large volatility," another commercial bank dealer said after the lev weakened to 83.70 per dollar two hours after opening around 82.50. 

 The lev closed at 81.60 on Wednesday. 

 Under central bank preliminary estimates foreign exchange reserves have fallen to $720 million in March from $1.27 billion at the end of 1995 following interest payments on Bulgaria's commercial and official foreign debt and interventions in support of the lev.

title: Bulgaria  forex  reserves fall to $703 million.
text:
SOFIA, April 18 (Reuter) - Bulgaria's foreign exchange reserves fell to $703 million at the end of March from $904 million a month earlier, central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov said on Thursday. 

 "At the end of last month the reserves stood at $703 million," Filipov told reporters. 

 "In the last few weeks we have bought $46 million," he said, adding that commercial banks had withdrawn some $30 million from their obligatory forex deposits and had not offered them on the market. 

 By June commercial banks must transfer their dollar-denominated minimum required reserves into levs, which will bring dollars onto the market, Filipov said. 

 The central bank is expected to buy the dollars offered and thus to increase its foreign exchange reserves. 

 Filipov said the central bank would rely on these dollars and on export earnings as well as its reserves to meet Brady coupon interest and other debt payments due in July. 

 Bulgaria's reserves have fallen from $1.3 billion since last December because of Brady coupon interest payments in January, interest payments to the Paris Club of official creditors and interventions in support of the lev. 

 Uncertainty over whether Bulgaria will clinch funding deals with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank have contributed to the downward pressure on the lev. 

 Keen to raise cash to cover this year's foreign debt payments totalling $1.2 billion, the government last week submitted a detailed reform plan to the two funding institutions. @ 

 Bulgaria's failure to meet reform targets -- including closing down loss-making state firms and restructuring its debt-laden banking sector -- has postponed funding agreements with the lending institutions for two years in a row. 

 A World Bank mission is currently visiting Sofia. 

 Filipov told reporters an IMF mission was expected in the Bulgarian capital early in May. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-328101

title: Bulgarian lev closes stronger at 77.10/30 vs dlr.
text:
SOFIA, March 7 (Reuter) - The Bulgarian lev strengthened to 77.10/30 per dollar at the close of the interbank forex market from 78.50-79.50 opening following a joint intervention by the central bank and Bulbank, dealers said. 

 "The rise in dollar supply boosted the lev", a commercial bank dealer said, adding that trade got livelier today as more banks and brokerages appeared in the market. 

 The lev traded in very small volumes near its yesterday's close between 78.50 and 79.50 per dollar at the opening and was headed to slide further when the central bank intervened at 77.99 in mid-morning. 

 Bulbank, Bulgaria's strongest, followed suit with sales of as much as $20 million at 77.95 levs and dollar supply rose further when some of the largest commercial banks began selling dollars, dealers said. 

 Most operators closed positions in the afternoon and the lev firmed to 77.10/30 per dollar in thin trade by the end of the day.

title: Central bank  buying pushes up  Bulgaria  lev - dealers.

SOFIA, Feb 21 (Reuter) - Large-scale intervention by the central bank helped push up the Bulgarian lev to 75.15/20 per dollar at the close on the interbank forex market, well above the opening 75.40, dealers said. 

 "Massive dollar sales by the central bank in the morning calmed down the market and strengthened the lev," a commercial bank dealer said. Operators said trade was active as many banks sought dollars for final clients and building of long positions. 

 The central bank launched dollar sales in early trade for the second day in a row to halt the lev fall. No details of the amounts sold were available. 

 The lev weakened to around 76.20 yesterday morning and seemed headed for a further fall before the intervention began. 

 Trade on the interbank money market was rather dull and thin as few banks offered lev funds, dealers said. 

 According to traders, banks with free levs channelled them to the interbank forex market, which further curbed supply to the money market. The interbank depo rate was flat on Tuesday's 45.4-45.5 percent.
